newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia denies reports on Bre-X geologist.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia denies reports on Bre-X geologist.

text.p: Indonesian authorities on Sunday denied a Canadian newspaper report that they had opened a murder investigation into the death of Filipino Michael de Guzman, former deputy chief geologist for Bre-X Minerals Ltd.

Brigadier-General Ahwil Luthan, secretary of Indonesia's National Central Bureau which handles investigations requiring Interpol assistance, said he had been misquoted by the Toronto Globe and Mail newspaper.
The newapaper, on its Saturday edition, quoted Luthan as saying that the case was being reopened and the chief of police had discussed the probe with the Philippines ambassador.
"I think I have been misquoted," he told Reuters. "There has not been any evidence that it is a murder case. All the evidence we have points to a suicide."
Luthan added, however, that investigations into de Guzman's death had not been closed.
"What I can say is that we are still investigating. Until now we believe it is a suicide case...there could be other evidence which could come out later."
De Guzman plunged to his death from a helicopter on March 26 in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province near Bre-X's Busang gold project.
Busang was once touted as the biggest gold find of the century, but independent auditors last week concluded it contained virtually no gold.
They said the Bre-X test samples had been tampered with on a massive scale. Canadian police have begun an investigation into the affair in an attempt to determine who was responsible.
Luthan said he had held talks with an official from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) on laying the groundwork for investigations but would give no details.
